title: Polynomially bounded emission fuel
statement: For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet and all natural-number parameters $C,e,c,A,d$, the function $n\mapsto n+(k+3)T(n)+k+1$ is polynomially bounded, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$ and $T(n)=c\bigl(A(n+C(n+1)^e+1)^d+1\bigr)^2$. Moreover, the function sending a bit string $x$ to the little-endian binary representation of this quantity at $n=|x|$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine $M$ over the binary alphabet
replaced: For every source machine and parameters, the last-round function of the input length is polynomially bounded, and the function sending an input to the binary representation of its last-round value is polynomial-time computable; the fuel is the last round index, read from an actual unary producer followed by the native binary length machine.
